object_description: terraced and staggered one-to-three-story school structure
design_condition: The structure follows the gently sloping topography, stays close to the existing building, and extends the ensemble through related outdoor rooms, alleys, arcades, and preserved play areas.

positive.statement: The differentiated scale and compositional balance establish a convincing connection to the existing complex and park.
The open-air school concept creates a wide range of teaching possibilities and gives the place a characteristic identity.
The concise building structure provides high practical value in the transition from outside to inside.
The free-standing pavilion offers great benefit to the district as a continuation of the ensemble.
Space, structure, light, rhythm, and proportion grow together in a joyful interplay.
The partial basement appropriately responds to the unfavorable subsoil and high groundwater level.
The interaction of classrooms, open-air rooms, and covered zones provides varied learning and work spaces.
The day school can be ideally divided into zones for younger and older children.
The use of wood in the construction and the green roof enables achievement of the ECO standard.

negative.statement: The fragmentary model negates the true dimensions of the expansive open volumes and raises doubts about scale and urban planning classification.
The generous spatial offer sometimes comes at the expense of rooms that are too small.
The close interconnection of the spatial offerings leads to a somewhat confusing access situation.
The location of the day school somewhat limits the overview of the area.
Balconies and terraces reduce daylight and limit passive solar use in winter.
A consistent installation and building technology concept is not apparent, and access is not guaranteed throughout.
The effort required to achieve the energy standard across the project is great.
The large external floor areas result in comparatively high construction and maintenance costs.
